1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 d5 3.cxd5 Nxd5 4.g3 g6 5..strategy: Develops with gain of time: d5 is now attacked by bishop and knight and guarded only by the queen, so Black has to answer at once. White wins the opening skirmish for the long diagonal.

Retreats and keeps the pieces on, avoiding an exchange that would hand White a pawn on c3 and an open b-file. Black keeps a compact position and the plan of the fianchetto, at the cost of time and a less active knight.
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 d5 3.cxd5 Nxd5 4.g3 g6 5..name: English Opening: Anglo-Indian Defence, Anglo-Grünfeld Variation

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 d5 3.cxd5 Nxd5 4.g3 g6 5..strategy: Trades off the attacked knight, so White normally recaptures with the b-pawn. Black spends no time on a retreat and can put the bishop on g7 against the new pawn on c3; White gets a broad pawn centre and an open b-file to work with.
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 d5 3.cxd5 Nxd5 4.g3 g6 5..name: English Opening: Anglo-Indian Defence, Anglo-Grünfeld Variation
